content.title: NCAA Tournament Sweet 16: 2-seed UConn men’s basketball vs. 3-seed Michigan State | 9:45 p.m., CBS
content.text: UConn men’s basketball (31-5) will look to get one step closer to getting to Indianapolis this weekend, as the Huskies are set to take on 3-seed Michigan State (27-7) in the Sweet 16 on Friday night at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C.The Spartans finished tied for second in the Big Ten regular-season standings, falling in the quarterfinals of the conference tournament to UCLA, the same team that UConn defeated in the Round of 32. Hall of Famer and head coach Tom Izzo has a well-constructed and veteran roster, led by All-American point guard Jeremy Fears Jr., and are fresh off a win over Louisville in Buffalo on Saturday. The Spartans rank No. 9 in KenPom and have the 22nd-ranked offense in the country.The Huskies sit at No. 11 in KenPom and knocked off the Bruins on Sunday in Philadelphia behind a career night from Alex Karaban and another double-double from Tarris Reed Jr. Dan Hurley has guided the Huskies to at least 31 wins for the third time since taking over the program, the previous two times ended in a national championship. The biggest storyline to come out of the last win for UConn was the return of Silas Demary Jr., who missed the first round game against Furman before playing 22 minutes against UCLA.The past five times that UConn has advanced to the second weekend, it has at minimum moved on to the Final Four. The last time that a second weekend appearance didn’t end with the Huskies cutting down the nets to move on was in 2006 against George Mason.Should the Huskies advance, they’d face either 1-seed Duke or 5-seed St. John’s in the Elite Eight on Sunday.Date/Time: Friday, March 27, 2026, approximately 9:45 p.m.Odds: UConn -1.5, over/under 134.5Location: Capital One Arena — Washington, DCKenPom Predicted Score: UConn 70, MSU 69Series HistoryThe Huskies and Spartans have played eight times, splitting the series 4-4. They’ve played twice in the NCAA Tournament, with Michigan St. defeating UConn in the Final Four in Detroit in 2009 and the Huskies returning the favor by knocking off the Spartans in the Elite Eight in 2014 at MSG. The last time the two teams faced off in a game that counted, Michigan State won 60-54 in the 2021 Battle 4 Atlantis despite double-doubles from both Adama Sanogo and Tyrese Martin.Availability reportSilas Demary Jr. and Jaylin Stewart were both listed as questionable for the matchup with UCLA and went through warmups. While Demary Jr. played 21 minutes coming off the bench, Stewart did not get in the game. As of the injury report that came out at 9 p.m. on Thursday night, there was no one listed on UConn’s side. The next one comes out two hours before game time as the NCAA has mandated the injury reports during the postseason.What to Watch ForFamiliar foes… sort ofBack in October, as you may recall, UConn and Michigan State faced off in a preseason exhibition contest in Hartford. The Huskies knocked off the Spartans 76-69 in the “scrimmage” and led wire-to-wire, but there are tons of things to dissect from the game that both teams have improved on.For starters, both Tarris Reed Jr. and Braylon Mullins were sidelined in the exhibition due to their preseason injuries. Eric Reibe and Jaylin Stewart started in their place. The Huskies being without two of their more impactful players and still defeating a good team certainly matters, but it should be taken with a grain of salt, seeing it was a preseason game.“There’s a couple key pointers that you can remember,” Karaban said, thinking back to that exhibition game. “Obviously, the personnel, too. I mean, they’re so different from October to March, just like we are, how much better they’ve gotten. I mean, their freshmen have gotten better. Everybody on their roster has been playing better than obviously they have in October.”One area that both sides have certainly cleaned up is the foul department. UConn and Michigan State combined for 56 fouls in the 40-minute game that took 2 hours and 25 minutes. Hurley and Izzo agreed before the game to do six fouls instead of five, and Dwayne Koroma still managed to foul out in 10 minutes. Reibe, Silas Demary Jr., and Malachi Smith all had five fouls, which of course won’t cut it on Friday.How much a game that doesn’t count in October matters for a game that counts for everything in March probably isn’t much, but it can’t hurt to have seen how you, in some form, match up with the personnel and have film to watch firsthand.Have no Fear(s), Silas is here!If Silas Demary Jr. wasn’t healthy going into this game against Michigan State, the odds of the Huskies pulling off the win would be in the gutter. Having one of the top playmakers and distributors in the country in Fears on the other side, it benefits to have one of the nation’s top perimeter defenders on your team.“I think he’s a steady point guard,” Demary said of Fears. “He’s very good at getting in the paint, getting everybody shots, and getting his bigs the ball. I think he’s a very good defender. He pushes their pace a lot and gets it out in transition and runs.”Demary definitely didn’t look like his usual self in the win over UCLA, but was still able to muster out 22 minutes. Having a few extra days to rest and heal is huge this time of year, especially for such an active player on both ends.“I’m feeling a lot better the past couple days. A lot of rehab, a lot of treatment. Try to get me as close as I can back to 100%,” Demary said Thursday.Malachi Smith did an impressive job in Demary’s place in the starting lineup and figures to be a major factor the rest of the way, perhaps a bigger factor than everyone thought. Even with Smith’s emergence, having Demary as close to 100% as possible to counter the talent of Fears is crucial for Friday.Tourney Rubber MatchAs mentioned earlier, UConn and Michigan State have faced off twice in the NCAA Tournament, entering Friday, each in different circumstances that favored the winning team both times.Back in 2009, the Huskies lost to the Spartans in the Final Four, still to this day the lone time that the team has lost in that round. With the game being played in Detroit, it was basically a home game for Michigan State, and the Spartans used the crowd on the way to an 82-73 win. UConn had an uphill climb all postseason after star guard Jerome Dyson went down with a season-ending injury in February. Many Husky fans to this day believe that the team would have won the national title if not for Dyson’s injury.In 2014, UConn got revenge in the Elite Eight. Shabazz Napier and Ryan Boatright carried the 7-seed Huskies past the Spartans at Madison Square Garden to punch their ticket to the Final Four. Spartans fans weren’t happy at having to play a lower seed in the Elite Eight in essentially their backyard, but with the heart that that team was playing with, the game could have been in East Lansing, and I’d still trust Napier and Co. to pull it out.This brings us to Friday, the “rubber match” if you will, in NCAA Tournament games between two of the 10 greatest programs in the sport. Whatever happens, expect it to be memorable one way or another.Physical battleThe biggest key for both sides to move on to the Elite Eight has to be rebounding and physicality down low. For as great as Fears has been, the anchor of Michigan State on both ends is the frontcourt duo of Carson Cooper and Jaxon Kohler. They combine to grab 16 rebounds per game and make life challenging for opponents on the defensive end. Kohler is more of a three-point threat, really developing into a shooter the past two years, while Cooper does most of his work back to the basket.We know what Reed can do, so there’s no sense in breaking down his game as in-depth. One big key for Reed is his ability to stay on the floor. Reibe does have the experience head-to-head against these guys, but ideally you have Reed out there as often as possible. Not just because he’s an explosive and talented player, but also because of his veteran presence, and has the benefit of having faced the Spartans a few times while playing for Michigan.“They’re going to try to set the tone early,” Reed said. “The game is going to be won on the boards and the defensive end. Whoever gets the most defensive rebounds and defends well will win the game. I feel like we’ve been doing a good job the last two games, crashing the glass. That’s not going to change for us.”Know your limitsThe biggest takeaway from a negative standpoint was the perimeter shooting from two of the Huskies’ best three-point shooters in Braylon Mullins and Solo Ball. The duo combined to go 3-25 from deep in the two games, with Mullins going 2-14 and Ball going 1-11. Do some quick math, that adds up to 12% on the dot.Let’s just put it this way: If Mullins and Ball combine to shoot 12% from three this weekend, this weekend will be the last weekend.“When you have a bunch of different players that are capable of doing so many different things, you just got to feed the hot hand,” Ball said Thursday.The hot hands so far have been Reed and Karaban, taking over games and accounting for the top two single-game scoring outputs from Husky players this season. Ball and Mullins have been in reduced roles as a result, especially Ball, after only playing 13 minutes against UCLA. Hurley is clearly aware that if Ball isn’t making shots, he’s a negative asset and shouldn’t be on the floor.For Mullins, if his threes don’t fall early in the game, look for him to be more of a factor in the mid-range area, an area he’s excelled in all year. Mullins is second in the country in field goal percentage on non-rim two pointers, so why not use this to your advantage as opposed to empty possessions on missed threes that can turn into fastbreak opportunities? And against the Spartans, they will.
